newsitem.title: USA: NYS Assembly delaying LIPA vote seen "legitimate".
newsitem.headline: NYS Assembly delaying LIPA vote seen "legitimate".

text.p: A senior aide to New York State Gov George Pataki on Thursday said the Assembly's decision to delay a key ruling on a partial state takeover of Long Island Lighting Co was justified.

"I think we would have preferred that they take it up...the ratepayers on Long Island are long overdue savings on electric bills," said Zenia Mucha, a senior aide and director of communications for the Republican governor.
She added: "This was not a political postponement, but a legitimate one."
Long Island residents pay some of the highest rates in the nation and Pataki has said the deal would cut their bills by more than 20 percent over five years.

The Democrat-controlled Assembly asked the state Public Authorities Control Board to delay until June 18 taking up the deal, which includes having the Long Island Power Authority buy assets from LILCO and Brooklyn Union Gas, who plan to merge.

Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan has questioned various aspects of the transaction, including the $7.3 billion of tax-exempt bond sales that would pay for it. A spokesman for Silver said on Wednesday the Assembly asked the authority to drop the deal from its agenda because it needed more time to gather data as neither it nor the state authority had finished holding hearings.
Silver, along with Pataki and the Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, make up the three-member board of the state authority, which means they each hold veto power.
LILCO's chairman, W.J. Catacosinos, has warned that the window for the deal is rapidly closing because it hinges on getting a tax exemption.

The IRS is expected to publish any day now new rules governing mergers between taxable and tax-exempt entities, which would go into effect 30 days later. Under those regulations, LIPA would face a $2 billion capital gains tax, an expense it is unwilling to incur.
